summary:
## Overview
This tutorial teaches two different ways to play **Justin Bieber's "Ghost"** on acoustic guitar, covering all rhythm parts and the distinctive lead guitar lick from the intro and bridge.

## Playing Method 1: No Capo (Original Key)

### Verse & Chorus
*   **Chords**: B minor → G → D → A
*   **Progression**: The four chords repeat.
*   **Strumming**: A 16th-note pattern is used (`Down up down up down up down up down down up`).

> [!TIP]
> When changing from **B minor** to **G**, you can use your index finger on the 2nd fret of the A-string as a **pivot point** to make the transition smoother.

### Pre-Chorus
*   **Chord Progression 1**: E minor 7 → D/F# → G
*   **Chord Progression 2**: G → B minor 7 → A
*   **Strumming**: A different pattern is used (`Down down up up down`).

## Playing Method 2: Capo on 2nd Fret (Easier)
This version uses simpler open chord shapes, making it more accessible for beginners.

### Verse & Chorus
*   **Chords**: A minor → F → C → G
*   **Strumming**: Uses the same 16th-note pattern as the no-capo version.

> [!NOTE]
> The instructor recommends an easier **F chord** fingering that uses the thumb to fret the low E string, avoiding a full barre.

### Pre-Chorus
*   **Chord Progression 1**: D minor → C/E → F
*   **Chord Progression 2**: F → A minor → G
*   **Strumming**: Uses the `Down down up up down` pattern.

## Strumming Patterns
Two primary strumming patterns are used throughout the song:

*   **Verse/Chorus Pattern**: `↓ ↑ ↓ ↑ ↓ ↑ ↓ ↑ ↓ ↓ ↑`
*   **Pre-Chorus Pattern**: `↓ ↓ ↑ ↑ ↓`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The timing of the chord changes is crucial. In the verse/chorus, the change happens on the 3rd beat. In the pre-chorus, changes happen on the first up-strum and the final down-strum.

## Lead Guitar Lick (Intro & Bridge)
*   This melodic part is played high on the neck, primarily using the **5th, 7th, and 8th frets** of the G, B, and high E strings.
*   Key techniques include hammer-ons (5th to 7th fret on the high E string) and slides (7th to 8th and back on the B string).
*   The lick is broken down into four distinct bars for easy learning.

## Introduction

Good day guys, my name is Dave and welcome to another Guitar Zed Hero song tutorial. In this lesson I'm going to teach you how to play Ghost by Justin Bieber. This is a really great and easy song. I'll teach you two different ways of playing it.

The first method is without a capo and the second method is slightly easier and you'll need a capo on the second fret for that second version. I'll also teach you how to play the intro and Bridge lead lick.

Now, if you want to master your chords back to front, then be sure to head over to guitarzhero.com to pick up my free guitar ebook. Or if you want to improve any guitar in general, then sign up to guitar zero hero premium, which is my complete step-by-step guitar course. Let's jump into the lesson.

## No-Capo Version: Verse & Chorus

Okay, so first off, I'll teach you how to play this song without a capo. Now for the verse and the chorus, it's a nice and easy four chord chord progression. We have a B minor chord, which looks like this. So index finger on the second fret of the fifth string, ring and pinky on the fourth frets of the fourth and third strings, and your middle finger on the third fret of the second string. And ideally, if you can also use your index finger to push down that second fret of the first string. So that's B minor. Our second chord is a G chord, then we have a D chord, and then an A chord.

Now our strumming pattern is going to go something like this. It's a 16th note strumming pattern and it sounds like: down up down up down up down up down down up. And in succession: down up down up down up down up down down up, down up down up down up down up down down up.

Now for each pattern, there's going to be two chords within that pattern, and the point at which we'll change chords is on the highlighted down strum, or the 'and' bit after the two. So from the B minor to the G: down up down up down up down up down down up. Now when you're transitioning from the B minor to the G, you can use your index finger as a pivot point. So going from here to here, just pivot around that index finger on that second fret of the fifth string. And then the same thing occurs from the D to the A. We change chords at the same point.

We put that all together and the verse and the chorus just sounds like this. Another tip is that you could also play your A chord like this by just barring your index finger across the second fret of the fourth, third and second strings. That will make it a tad easier for you to transition back to the B minor and that would look like this.

## No-Capo Version: Pre-Chorus

The next part we need to learn is just the pre-chorus, which is really nice and easy. There's an E minor 7. So it's the same as an E minor chord, except you put your ring and pinky finger on the third frets of the first and second. So that's our E minor 7.

And then I'm going to go to a D/F#. So lift your index and middle finger and put them on the second frets of the sixth and third string, and you can lift your pinky finger as well and just mute that first string. That's D/F#, and then we go to a G.

Now those three chords are contained within one strumming pattern and that goes: down down up up down. Now there's two points where we change chords. The first is on that up strum, the first up strum. And then on the final down strum. And in total...

And for the second set of chords we have G, B minor 7. So from the G, you're going to lift your middle finger and put it on the second fret of the third string. So that's B minor 7. You can leave that fourth string open. And then our final chord is an A. We have the exact same strumming pattern, so: down down up up down. And the points at which we change chords are the same as well. And the pre-chorus in total. And that's it for all the rhythm parts with the no capo version.

## Capo Version: Verse & Chorus

Okay, so if you want a slightly easier way of playing this, then we can put a capo on the second fret of our guitar like so. Now our verse chords are A minor, and then we have an F chord. So you're going to play a full F bar chord like this, or you can play it like this, which is my preferred method. It's a bit easier to transition to the other chords. So ring and pinky finger on the third frets of the fifth and fourth string, middle finger on that second fret of the third, and index finger on the first fret of the second string. And ideally if you can reach over your thumb and hit the first fret of the sixth string. So that's our F chord. And then we have C and then G. So those are our four chords.

Now our strumming pattern is the same as well. So it's just: down up down up down up down up down down up. And the point which we change chords, 'and' bit after two. So the verse and the chorus with a capo...

## Capo Version: Pre-Chorus

For our pre-chorus, we've got one line of chords here. We start with the D minor and then a C/E, so it's a C chord but you can hit the open sixth string, and then an F chord.

Now our strumming pattern is: down down up up down. And the points at which we change chords are highlighted down below. So the first set of chords... For our second set of chords it's our F, A minor, and then a G. And the strumming pattern is the same: down down up up down. So the pre-chorus with the capo...

## How to Play the Lead Lick

Okay, so now I'll teach you the lead guitar part, which is in the intro and also the bridge of the song. So it's really simple. There's one line of tab here. We're going to start in this position. So middle and ring finger on the seventh frets of the third and second string. So you'll pluck the third string, second string, and then index finger goes up to the fifth fret of the first string. And those are our lead-in notes, plucked at eighth notes, so: and four and.

For our next bar, you're going to pluck that first string again and hammer on to the seventh fret. And then with your free middle finger, go onto the seventh fret of the second string, and back to the fifth fret of the first string. And then we end with the seventh fret of the third string twice. So that second bar...

For this next bar, we're going to pluck that fifth fret of the first string, and then we have a three note run. So you pluck that fifth fret again, eighth fret of the second string to pinky, and then seventh fret. So those are the three notes. After that three note run, we hit the fifth fret of the second string and end with the seventh fret of the third string twice. And the bar in total...

For this final bar, you take your ring finger, put it on the seventh fret of the second string, hit that twice. And then seventh fret of the third. And then back to the seventh fret of the second, hit it and slide up to eighth, then back down to seventh fret, and end on the seventh fret of the third string. So the final bar... and the whole riff in total.

## Full Playthrough Demonstrations

And those are all the parts of this song. So now I'll be doing two playthroughs of this song. The first playthrough will be without a capo, and the second playthrough will be with a capo and that's slightly easier to play. Big thanks to my friend Eric for lending his awesome vocals for this playthrough. Feel free to play this back as many times as you'd like, to practice play along to and see how you go.

Thanks so much for watching. If you've enjoyed this lesson then I know you'll absolutely love these other lessons too so hit the link here. Or if you want to grab a copy of my free guitar ebook then head over to guitarzhero.com or click the link here. Thanks so much and I'll see you guys next time on Guitar Zed Hero. Cheers.
